analysis: The closest remains a substantial AI/cognition response: programming, logic, algorithms, probability, machine learning/deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimisation and robotics connect to neural, perceptual, language and social-cognitive study. The target relationship rests on this academic substance, not merely coherence or a transparent limitation.

Five substitutions improve specific contributions: closest replaces clinical Health Psychology with Social Psychology and persuasive climate communication with reinforcement learning; computational replaces persuasive communication with Brain and Behaviour foundations; cognitive replaces Lifespan Development with empirical data workflows and persuasive communication with Style and Meaning. Each removed course was read and considered: clinical patient-care and life-span breadth are valid psychology, but weaker here than the selected social-agent/data roles. Climate persuasion is not HCI. Linear Systems was considered for control, but thirteen spring-only courses would exceed twelve spring slots in the computational palette. Brain foundations provide a stronger specific cognitive-model connection than the removed communication course, while keeping the computational priority.

Computational AI is materially organised around software, advanced algorithms, structured data, networks and numerical mathematics, with learning/vision/robotics. Cognitive/language is organised around neural and psychological functions, mind/agency, meta-analysis and grammatical/discourse interpretation while retaining quantitative and computational tools. Four actual course changes separate closest from cognitive; other pairs exceed that floor. Ethical and responsible design remains a separate assessed direction after the maximum, not a catch-all label or a claim that one ethics course makes the whole option human-centred design.

All current selected course profiles or official descriptions received substantive consideration. Description-only Psycholinguistics, Perception and Action, reinforcement learning and relational databases count fully within stated scope. Psycholinguistics is scheduled in its only planned Spring-2027 slot after Brain and Behaviour. Neurobiology is comparative/regulatory foundation, not the strongest advanced cognition match. Meta-analysis is evidence synthesis, not a newly conducted empirical study. Style and Meaning supplies close linguistic interpretation, not NLP algorithms.

Rebuilt all schedules from actual covered term columns, repairing the legacy offering conflicts without extrapolation or editing Excel. Formal prerequisites precede every dependent course, four courses occupy each term, PPD is first-year, all options contain 24 unique courses and at least six advanced courses. Programming precedes vision, data work precedes ML, ML precedes deep learning, brain foundation precedes advanced cognition; the computational option puts research methods before behavioural statistics and algorithms before advanced algorithms. These preferences are not invented hard prerequisites.

Seventeen bounded alignments use actual content. Search/optimisation fits AI1; reinforcement learning fits one strand of AI2; higher cognitive functions is the strongest neuroscience relationship; psycholinguistics fits the first-year human-language unit rather than NLP. Research Methods fits introductory statistics, behavioural models fit Statistics II. Eight explicit gaps retain critical/scientific thinking, HCI, agent-based simulation, the research workshop, mobility, hybrid intelligence, NLP and the thesis. Optional independent research remains additional to the scheduled 180 EC.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: develops academic writing, critical reading, collaborative inquiry and reflective practice for the common first-year foundation

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: directly supplies research design, sampling, statistical analysis and an empirical project, preparing the computational alternative for quantitative evaluation

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: directly studies AI ethics through philosophical and psychological questions, including human agency and AI in social, organisational and care relationships

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.contribution: directly develops probabilistic inference and decisions through Bayesian and temporal beliefs, Markov decision processes, partial observability, bandits and multi-agent decision problems

DISARIN212.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
DISARIN212.contribution: directly supplies proof, sets, Boolean logic, functions, induction and discrete reasoning for AI and algorithm design

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI
DISARIN311.contribution: directly develops heuristic and adversarial search, constraint satisfaction and linear/discrete optimisation, with algorithm experiments for intelligent problem solving

DISARIN312.name: Reinforcement Learning
DISARIN312.contribution: directly studies reinforcement learning and implementation of neural agents that learn through trial and error in an environment

DISCOMP211.name: Networks & Operating Systems
DISCOMP211.contribution: complements autonomous and computational AI through network protocols, processes, concurrency, memory and resource management for communicating software systems

DISCOMP212.name: Database Management Systems
DISCOMP212.contribution: complements AI implementation through relational data models, SQL, normalisation, authorisation and querying for structured training and research data

DISCOMP213.name: Software Development
DISCOMP213.contribution: directly develops software design, multiple programming paradigms, testing and maintainability, including C++ and Haskell

DISCOMP311.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
DISCOMP311.contribution: directly studies searching, sorting, string and graph algorithms, complexity and experimental performance analysis for AI implementation

DISCOMP312.name: Advanced Algorithms
DISCOMP312.contribution: directly extends computational methods through algebraic algorithms, hashing, Fourier transforms, greedy and dynamic programming and network flow

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: directly supplies reproducible data cleaning, joining, visualisation and project work in R for the empirical data used by cognitive research and machine learning

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: directly develops regression, classification, resampling, regularisation, trees, support-vector machines and unsupervised learning with empirical R/Python work

DISDATA212.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
DISDATA212.contribution: directly studies image filtering, segmentation, tracking and classification through Python/OpenCV pipelines for machine perception

DISDATA311.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
DISDATA311.contribution: directly develops neural-network models and Python deep-learning implementations, including image, text and sequential-data applications

DISDATA312.name: Robotics
DISDATA312.contribution: directly studies robot motion, grasping, kinematics, geometry and collision planning through robot-arm work; sensing and control support the embodied-systems strand

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: directly supplies Python programming, conditions, loops, functions, recursion, data structures, object-oriented work and testing for computational problem solving

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: directly supplies calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic modelling that support learning algorithms and quantitative cognition

DISMATH211.name: Linear Algebra
DISMATH211.contribution: directly supplies vector spaces, eigenvalues, least squares, singular-value decomposition and dimensional reduction for computational models and learning

DISMATH213.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
DISMATH213.contribution: complements model implementation through numerical differential equations, root finding, interpolation and analysis of approximation error and stability

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.contribution: directly supplies probability distributions, inference, Bayesian reasoning and sampling algorithms for uncertainty and computational models

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: directly investigates mind, consciousness, physicalism, virtual worlds and possible artificial minds, grounding the cognitive alternative philosophically

GOSPHIL313.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
GOSPHIL313.contribution: complements cognitive AI through philosophical analysis of agency, free will and determinism alongside scientific accounts of action

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: complements cognitive inquiry through comparative neuroanatomy, neural regulation, biological rhythms and sleep, rather than replacing advanced cognitive neuroscience

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: directly studies neural mechanisms of sensory processing, perception and action, including cognitive-neuroscience methods

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: directly studies attention, memory, emotion, control, social cognition and consciousness, including an attention experiment and research proposal

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: directly studies psychological and neural mechanisms of language comprehension, production, acquisition, bilingualism and meaning; it provides human-language foundations rather than a full computational-linguistics course

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: directly introduces neuropsychology, neural signalling, learning and research methods, providing a biological and behavioural foundation for cognitive AI questions

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: directly supplies social cognition, attitudes, influence and group behaviour for understanding human agents and social interaction in cognitive AI

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: directly supplies experimental design, multivariable and latent-variable models, R analysis and scientific reporting for behavioural data

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: directly supplies systematic review, meta-analysis, effects, bias and moderator analysis in R for evaluating cognitive and behavioural research; it does not claim to collect a new experimental dataset

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: complements language and cognition through grammatical, stylistic and discourse analysis of literary and nonfiction texts, adding interpretation of meaning rather than automated language processing

alignment.rationale: Both introduce statistical reasoning, empirical analysis and research data. Tilburg specifically teaches R with chi-square tests, t-tests, ANOVA and regression; UCR adds research design, sampling and a project.

Both apply moral reflection to AI and its consequences for human values and responsibility. UCR connects this to psychological, social and care relationships; Tilburg develops moral theories, justice and philosophy of technology.
Both teach formal reasoning and sets. Tilburg develops truth-functional and first-order logic and natural deduction; UCR places logic within a broader discrete-mathematics programme.

Both use search algorithms to solve AI problems. UCR develops heuristic, adversarial and constrained optimisation more deeply; Tilburg combines this with AI history, philosophy and an introduction to uncertainty.

Both address reinforcement learning and agents learning from experience. UCR concentrates on this strand; Tilburg surveys several further fields, including neural networks, language, vision and robotics.

Both develop functional and object-oriented programming and maintainable software design. Tilburg centres advanced Python, concurrency and design patterns; UCR works across C++ and Haskell with software development practice.
Both study searching, sorting, data structures and algorithm performance. UCR also develops string and graph algorithms and experimental comparison.
Both implement and evaluate machine-learning models for regression, classification and unsupervised learning using Python and related tools.
Both study neural networks, training and practical deep-learning models, including image, sequential and language applications.

Both study robots through perception, action and control. UCR focuses on robot-arm geometry, kinematics and motion planning; Tilburg emphasises cognitive and social robotics and a social autonomous agent.
Both develop Python programming and algorithmic problem solving through variables, conditions, loops, functions and data structures.
Both teach calculus and its quantitative applications. UCR also includes complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic models.
Both develop vectors, matrices, linear spaces, transformations and eigenvalues for quantitative and computational applications.
Both connect attention, memory, emotion, decision and control with neural systems and investigative methods, including practical experiments. Their selected topics and methods differ.
Both examine language acquisition and processing through cognitive, psychological and neural mechanisms. Tilburg additionally reviews cognitive and computational models of language.

Both introduce relationships among cognition, behaviour and brain function. UCR centres neuropsychology; Tilburg integrates this with philosophy, computation, language and other cognitive-science disciplines.
Both analyse relationships in behavioural data using statistical models and R. Tilburg develops generalised and mixed-effect models; UCR adds experimental design and latent-variable analysis.
Critical evaluation supports several selected courses, but none is placed here as the dedicated study of reasoning biases, rationality and philosophy of science.
Human cognition and social interaction provide relevant foundations, but no selected course provides the dedicated interface design, task analysis and usability evaluation taught here.
Probabilistic and multi-agent decisions contribute related ideas, but no selected course centres the design, validation and simulation of agent-based models taught here.
Methods, data projects and evidence synthesis support research. None is counted again as this separate full-cycle group experiment or machine-learning investigation.
Thirty credits remain open for approved partner-university study; no destination or course package is invented.

Learning algorithms and cognitive inquiry provide foundations, but no selected course centres knowledge-based recurrent networks, symbolic explainability and human-in-the-loop collaborative pipelines.

Psycholinguistics and stylistic analysis study human language and meaning. No selected course provides the dedicated tokenisation, tagging, parsing, distributional semantics and NLP implementation taught here.
The supervised empirical quantitative CSAI thesis remains a separate requirement. Optional UCR independent research is shown outside the scheduled 180 credits.
